description: base.regression on the core, as python-core recorded it at T1.11d: describe_source's, materialize's and predict's inputs (predict's request state as the host handed it back), every fetch the core asked for with its plan (the step trace), the SourceDescription describe_source answered, the request state materialize answered (its version, the query and the payload, each number as the text the core wrote), and predict's answer: the call the core wrote for the endpoint, each number as its text, with the value of metadata.request_id left out and its type kept (decision E35, approved by the owner on 2026-10-10, contract/compare-policy.yaml's one exclusion: the host draws that id at random), the model, call id and metadata the endpoint gave, and the result's rows, each float as its IEEE-754 bits. sdm-testkit's tests/duckdb_provider.rs holds rust-host to it and contract/tests/test_schema_route.py, test_materialize_route.py and test_predict_route.py hold python-core to it, so CI gates the two hosts' equality until T1.18's comparator does. From T1.21d the description is the schema as the core assembles it (the link inferred by name, each column's stype_before_key and each table's edit_stamp_refused, from T1.23 time_column_inferred; decision E55), and materialize's schema is that description on both hosts: rust-host's its own, the case naming none. From T1.23 each described table names the source table it reads (source, decision E59), on both hosts.

statements.text: SELECT table_name FROM duckdb_tables() WHERE NOT temporary AND NOT internal AND database_name = current_database() AND schema_name = current_schema()

SELECT constraint_type, constraint_column_names
FROM duckdb_constraints()
WHERE table_name = 'orders'
  AND database_name = current_database() AND schema_name = current_schema()

SELECT constraint_type, constraint_column_names
FROM duckdb_constraints()
WHERE table_name = 'users'
  AND database_name = current_database() AND schema_name = current_schema()

SELECT constraint_index, referenced_table,
       constraint_column_names, referenced_column_names
FROM duckdb_constraints()
WHERE table_name = 'orders'
  AND database_name = current_database() AND schema_name = current_schema()
  AND constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY'

SELECT constraint_index, referenced_table,
       constraint_column_names, referenced_column_names
FROM duckdb_constraints()
WHERE table_name = 'users'
  AND database_name = current_database() AND schema_name = current_schema()
  AND constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY'

SELECT 0 AS k, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT "order_id") AS d, COUNT(CASE WHEN "order_id" IS NULL THEN 1 END) AS z
FROM "orders"
UNION ALL
SELECT 1 AS k, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT "user_id") AS d, COUNT(CASE WHEN "user_id" IS NULL THEN 1 END) AS z
FROM "users"

SELECT
  0 as table_index,
  MIN(CAST("ts" AS TIMESTAMP)) as min_date,
  MAX(CAST("ts" AS TIMESTAMP)) as max_date
FROM "orders"

SELECT "user_id"
FROM (SELECT * FROM "users"
WHERE "user_id" IS NOT NULL)
USING SAMPLE reservoir(10000 ROWS) REPEATABLE (42)

SELECT s."batch" AS "__kumo_batch__", t."price", t."ts"
FROM "__sdm_seeds__" s
JOIN "orders" t
  ON t."user_id" = s."key"
 AND CAST(t."ts" AS TIMESTAMP) <= s."end"
 AND CAST(t."ts" AS TIMESTAMP) > s."start"

SELECT s."batch" AS "__kumo_batch__", COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY s."batch") AS "__kumo_matches__", t."user_id", t."age", t."country"
FROM "__sdm_seeds__" s
JOIN "users" t
  ON t."user_id" = s."key"
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY s."batch"
) = 1

SELECT s."batch" AS "__kumo_batch__", t."order_id", t."user_id", t."price", t."ts"
FROM "__sdm_seeds__" s
JOIN "orders" t
  ON t."user_id" = s."key"
 AND CAST(t."ts" AS TIMESTAMP) <= s."time"
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY s."batch"
  ORDER BY CAST(t."ts" AS TIMESTAMP) DESC NULLS LAST, t."order_id" ASC NULLS LAST
) <= 32
ORDER BY s."batch", CAST(t."ts" AS TIMESTAMP) DESC NULLS LAST, t."order_id" ASC NULLS LAST
